evidence: Caes. B.C. 3.47: nova et inūsitāta bellī ratiō (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Deiot. 1: inūsitātum est with a clause
Cic. de Or. 2.361: īnsolita mihi loquācitās (Lewis & Short)
Plin. Pan. 60.6: rārum ac prope īnsolitum est
terms.comment: Of people it means “unaccustomed to” (īnsolitus ad labōrem, Caes. B.C. 3.85); of things, “unusual”.

phrases.english: a new and unusual way of making war

phrases.latin: in prīncipe rārum ac prope īnsolitum est, ut sē putet obligātum
phrases.english: in a ruler it is rare and almost unheard of to think himself under an obligation

phrases.latin: Inūsitātum est tē tam mātūrē surgere.
phrases.english: It’s unusual for you to get up so early.
